strengths: The restrained black, parchment and ochre palette, literary serif typography and botanical plates form a highly specific identity for a serious coastal planting studio.
The plant register is more than decoration: seasonal bars, botanical names, condition labels and garden provenance turn expertise into a distinctive visual system.
The £450 first visit is consistently framed as a concrete, low-ambiguity product, with well-placed calls to action across long pages.

Mobile layouts are deliberately recomposed: featured specimens receive scale, secondary cards alternate image and copy, and project plant strips remain browsable without becoming generic stacked cards.
The gardens pages replace conventional portfolio photography with evidence—survival periods, irrigation reductions and replacement records—which credibly supports the studio's central claim.

defects.detail: Desktop body copy, metadata and plant captions are frequently too small and low-contrast relative to the large headings, making supporting evidence harder to absorb than it should be.
Calls to action are visible, but the repeated label does not explain what happens after booking or reduce practical uncertainty about availability, geography and scheduling at the moment of decision.
The mobile header has an awkward two-tier order—navigation first, then brand and CTA—and consumes substantial vertical space before the page proposition appears.

Some desktop sections, particularly the garden listings, carry unusually large empty areas while adjacent plant grids are dense; the rhythm occasionally shifts from editorial restraint into under-filled composition.

The visibly fictional email domain and explicit prototype disclaimer in the footer break the otherwise convincing commercial presentation and would materially reduce trust on a live client-facing site.

The antique plates are exceptionally appropriate, but repeated specimens across the hero, register and case studies create some visual redundancy and can make different projects feel less individually memorable.

summary: This is distinctive, strategically coherent work whose botanical register makes the studio's expertise and coastal specialization tangible without relying on garden photography. It clears a strong professional bar, though finer desktop typography, tighter spatial calibration and removal of prototype contact language are needed before it can operate at full commercial credibility.
